query: Starting from a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, what single intervention could overcome limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness while retaining or increasing strength? The hypothesis should address the tendency for dislocation pile-ups near internal boundaries to produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and catastrophic damage during straining. Specify the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted strength and ductility relative to the untreated starting material, the applicable testing and operating conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Phase-selective recrystallization (PSR) can overcome the limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness of a eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies, while retaining or increasing its strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Eutectic high-entropy alloy with a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies
generation.conditions: Room temperature, quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
generation.structural_mediator: Hierarchical microstructure with a skeletal, non-recrystallized B2 phase and a recrystallized FCC phase
generation.mechanism: PSR eliminates weak boundaries, prevents premature crack nucleation, and allows both phases to contribute to strain hardening simultaneously through high-density dislocation multiplication and a strain-induced B2 to BCT phase transformation
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved tensile ductility and strength, with a uniform elongation of ~30% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ~2.2 GPa
generation.baseline: As-cast alloy with limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittleness
generation.boundary: Room temperature, quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests
generation.uncertainty: Theoretical model for calculating the suitable deformation level for PSR is semi-quantitative and ignores information on microstructure and strain rate

falsification_experiment.design: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the PSR-treated alloy does not exhibit improved tensile ductility and strength compared to the as-cast alloy, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How can the limited ductility of eutectic high-entropy alloys (EHEAs) be overcome to achieve ultra-ductility while maintaining high strength?. System: Ni30Co30Cr10Fe10Al18W2 (at%) eutectic high-entropy alloy consisting of FCC and B2 phases; industrial A357 casting aluminum alloy. Processing: Two cycles of 30% cold rolling followed by annealing at 1200 °C for 20 mins with water quenching; for A357: two cycles of 15% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins followed by two cycles of 30% cold rolling at 540 °C for 40 mins. Test conditions: Quasi-static uniaxial tensile tests at room temperature with an initial strain rate of 1 × 10−3 s−1; in situ tensile tests in FE-SEM; loading-unloading-reloading tests for back stress measurement. Findings: The phase-selectively recrystallized (PSR) EHEA achieves a uniform elongation of ∼33% and an engineering ultimate tensile strength approaching ∼2.2 GPa.; The PSR EHEA exhibits a fracture true strain of ∼30%, which is double that of the As-cast (AC) alloy (∼14%) and the fully recrystallized (FR) alloy (∼17%).; The fracture true stress of the PSR EHEA reaches ∼1850 MPa, significantly higher than the AC (∼1390 MPa) and FR (∼1460 MPa)
